A.biggest_strength: A fully live, dynamic simulation engine with continuous sliders for learning rate and starting position, complete arithmetic transparency in a dedicated table, and side-by-side small multiples comparing all three learning rates at once.
A.biggest_weakness: The parabola plot marks steps with connected numbered circles rather than directional vector arrows along the curve, which would slightly enhance motion intuition.

B.biggest_strength: Rich conceptual depth in the supplementary notes connecting the 1D toy problem to real-world ML topics (curvature, mini-batch SGD noise, non-convex landscapes, and Adam), accompanied by color-coded mathematical notation.
B.biggest_weakness: Heavily constrained and pre-baked interactivity limited to a static 9-row JSON lookup table with no adjustable starting position or continuous learning rate control, alongside an aggressive intermediate rounding scheme that falsely suggests an about-right rate lands exactly on the minimum.
factual_errors: Scene 4 claims that the about-right learning rate (η = 0.3) 'lands on 3'. Mathematically, gradient descent on L(w) = (w - 3)² with η = 0.3 multiplies the distance to the minimum by 0.4 at each step, converging asymptotically towards 3 without ever reaching it in finite steps. It only reaches 3.00 in Page B because B rounds each intermediate step to 2 decimal places and feeds the rounded values into the next iteration, confusing a precision artifact with algorithmic convergence.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is significantly superior as an educational tool for course notes. It computes all numbers live, allowing students to freely adjust both the learning rate and starting position to explore the exact convergence regimes explained in the text. Its layout integrates the curve plot, loss chart, controls, and arithmetic table simultaneously on one screen without jarring scene swaps, and provides side-by-side small multiples for direct visual comparison. In contrast, Page B relies on a hardcoded 9-step lookup table across 5 rigid scenes, suffers from an auto-touring timer and text collisions, obscures scene titles on mobile, and introduces a conceptual error by claiming η = 0.3 lands exactly on the minimum.
